rationale: A wins because it gives the founder genuinely different reporting paths instead of dressing the same DTC-reversal thought in multiple jackets. “Glossier more than doubles its retail footprint, from 600 to 1,400 Sephora doors” is a clean trade-news angle; B’s “The brand that built the DTC playbook is now calling wholesale its fastest-growing channel” mostly replays its first wholesale/DTC angle with a louder tie. A still needs a factual scrub, but it does more strategic work.
gaps_in_A: “Glossier times its first fragrance launch to its biggest retail push yet” gets the product fact wrong: the update says first fragrance line extension, not first fragrance launch.
“built on saying no to stores” and “whole mythology was direct-only” overstate the supplied fact. DTC-only is grounded; anti-store ideology needs a source.

“Sephora at Kohl's becomes a test case for prestige beauty in a big-box mall” reaches past the update. “Test case” and the mass-market real-estate thesis need outside evidence before they can carry an angle.
“biggest retail push yet” is not established by the facts. The door count jump is real; the historical superlative is not.
gaps_in_B: “after a decade of treating retail as the enemy” is too cute and not grounded. The update says DTC-only, not hostile to retail.
The first two angles are padded cousins: “DTC-vs.-wholesale debate across the beauty category” and “DTC is a sustainable standalone model” are the same story at nearly the same altitude.
“The brand that built the DTC playbook” and “investor narrative” import outside context the update did not provide. If you want that frame, prove it instead of smuggling it in.

“No beauty or fragrance reporter can evaluate newsworthiness from this” throws away a viable fragrance-retail strategy angle. The product-only version is weak; the timing-with-Sephora version is not automatically dead.
